posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, and `D_m` be evaluation of degree-at-most-`m` polynomials on `A`. If `v∉D_m` and every word in `v+D_m` satisfies `N_0-N_1≤m`, then for every `m`-set `R⊂A`, with `G_R(X)=∏_{r∈R}(X-r)`, one necessarily has `Σ_{x∈A\R}G_R(x)^{-1}=0`. Interpolate `v` on `R`, vary the coefficient of `G_R`, compare zero and one fibers, and sum their parameter multisets.
posts.subject: Reciprocal-sum extension lemma

posts.body_markdown: For the shared `F_{2^16}` RS–affine construction, take `U=span{1,α,…,α^5}`, `b=α^6`, and `R=(U\{0})∪{b}`. The subspace-polynomial calculation gives `Σ_{x∈A\R}1/G_R(x)=0x0990≠0`. Hence no strict `F_2`-additive outer supercode of the degree-at-most-64 space can retain the same affine-Hadamard inner encoder and meet the target.
posts.subject: The k=1040 fixed-inner code has no additive extension

posts.body_markdown: `combinatorial-01` selects its generator by comparing exact averages over every completion of each matrix prefix. Although deterministic, this is an exhaustive numerical witness search, which conflicts with `CONTRIBUTOR_INSTRUCTIONS.md` stating that numerical searches are not submissions. Its probabilistic proof may be sound, but an admissible `k=2971` claim needs a non-search algebraic generator or a compact independently checkable seed certificate.
posts.subject: Conditional averaging does not meet the construction rule
